title: A Survey on the Linear Representation Hypothesis
abstract: arXiv:2609.22695v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The term "linear representation hypothesis" (LRH) has appeared across diverse subfields of artificial intelligence, neuroscience, and cognitive science. But previous works have not consistently treated the LRH as a falsifiable scientific hypothesis; we analyze these inconsistencies and examine their implications for how prior theoretical and methodological results should be interpreted. Based on this analysis, we argue that claims regarding linear representations become well-defined only through careful examination of the model, representation location, feature definition, and evaluation dataset. We therefore propose a more rigorous formalization of the LRH that makes these dependencies explicit and allows the hypothesis to be evaluated as a falsifiable scientific claim. Finally, we identify some non-trivial open problems that warrant further attention from the research community.

translated_abstract: “线性表示假设”（LRH）这一术语出现在人工智能、神经科学和认知科学的多个不同子领域中。然而，以往的研究并未始终如一地将LRH视为一个可证伪的科学假设；我们分析了这些不一致之处，并探讨了它们对如何解释先前的理论和方法论结果的影响。基于这一分析，我们认为，只有通过对模型、表示位置、特征定义和评估数据集进行仔细考察，关于线性表示的论断才能得到明确的定义。因此，我们提出了一个更严格的LRH形式化框架，使这些依赖关系显式化，并使该假设能够作为一个可证伪的科学论断加以评估。最后，我们指出了一些值得研究界进一步关注的非平凡开放问题。
tldr: 本文系统综述了线性表示假设（LRH），指出以往研究未将其作为可证伪科学假设一致对待的问题，并提出了一个将模型、表示位置、特征定义和评估数据集等依赖关系显式化的更严格形式化框架，使LRH能够被明确检验。
en_tdlr: This survey identifies inconsistencies in how prior work has treated the linear representation hypothesis (LRH) as a falsifiable scientific claim, and proposes a more rigorous formalization that makes explicit its dependencies on the model, representation location, feature definition, and evaluation dataset.
